text:
Maya Chen: heads-up — seeing a drain/reschedule loop hitting us-west2-gpu-rack-14, dozens of tiny pods bouncing, eviction spike and cost blip :eyes:
Sam Ortiz: ugh, logs? any common taint/affinity pattern?
Maya Chen: paste of kubelet log snippet:
```
I0320 14:12:04 kubelet evicting Pod default/model-trainer-7 due to NodeAffinityMismatch
I0320 14:12:05 scheduler Preempted pod model-trainer-7 -> bound to node usw2-gpu-14b
I0320 14:12:06 kubelet TaintAdded taint=reserved:NoSchedule on node usw2-gpu-14b
I0320 14:12:07 Pod model-trainer-7 evicted: TaintTolerationMismatch
```
Maya Chen: pattern: scheduler moves pod, node gets tainted immediately, pod evicted. repeat every ~20s.
Priya Nair: that sequence looks like something is flipping a rack-level taint after a reserve controller runs — any recent change to rack-reserve or node lifecycle hooks? :thinking_face:
Raj Patel: i pushed a change yesterday to autoset a "reserved" taint during our warm-pool trim to prevent user pods on warm nodes. Aim was to mark nodes while we drain pre-warm tasks. Might be a race.
Liza Gomez: can we repro with one node? I can run a targeted drain/observe, but we're seeing cost impact. How many pods affected?
Maya Chen: roughly 40 small jobs bounced in last 6m, many from low-priority queues. Some are latency-sensitive batch.
Sam Ortiz: query from prometheus? you'll see eviction rate and preempt count rising. Can you run `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Running` and filter?
Maya Chen: ran quick grep, attaching snippet: `kubectl get pods -A | grep Evicted | wc -l` -> 37 in last 5m.
deploy-bot: Deploy completed: infra/rack-reserve v2.3.1 by Raj Patel at 14:08 UTC
Priya Nair: ok that aligns — deploy triggered a job that annotates nodes to `reserved=true` then adds taint. Looks like the controller is marking nodes after the scheduler has placed pods -> causes TaintTolerationMismatch evictions.
Raj Patel: i can roll back the taint step, but need quick mitigation. Options: 1) have controller add taint before allowing new scheduling (pre-mark), 2) add toleration to low-priority pods (risky), 3) pause controller for us-west2.
Liza Gomez: pause sounds fastest. Can you toggle the controller flag?
Raj Patel: yes I can flip `rack-reserve.enabled=false` for usw2. Doing it now — will report in ~30s.
Maya Chen: noted — traffic dropping backlog is shrinking but some flapping remains.
Sam Ortiz: we should also add a short backoff so controller waits for node quiescent state before tainting. Otherwise rolling nodes will keep flipping.
Priya Nair: agreed. I'll open a scheduler ticket to add a hook: if node has pods bound in last Xs, delay taint/add toleration window. Also propose a small grace toleration for our own infra-managed jobs to avoid preemption thrash.
Maya Chen: quick ask — can someone scrub the affected pods to avoid restart storms? we should cordon and drain gracefully where possible.
Liza Gomez: on it — starting a manual cordon on the 3 flapping nodes, migrating workloads with `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60`.
Raj Patel: controller flag off. Monitoring.
deploy-bot: Alert: autoscaler detected surge in Evicted pods (threshold breached)
Maya Chen: eviction count down to single digits now. Thanks.
Priya Nair: filing ticket INF-3247: "rack-reserve taint ordering causes immediate evictions" with proposed fixes: pre-mark nodes, controller backoff, scheduler hook for toleration window. Assigning to Raj + scheduler.
Sam Ortiz: add a follow-up to run a small canary where controller taints in pre-mark mode for 1 rack, validate no evictions for 10m.
Raj Patel: will run canary tomorrow US morning after QA signoff.
Liza Gomez: thumbs up. Postmortem note: tag impacted pods and include cost delta in incident doc.
Maya Chen: thanks all — saving logs and metrics, will add to the ticket. :thumbsup:
